> **November 24 release reconciliation:** Scoring v0.5 with data-v0.7 ranks Charlotte #18 of 190 (88.82; displayed as 88.8). The scoring configuration and saved outputs reflect PR #140. The scoring run uses an industry filter minimum of 0 and exports both raw share and percentile.


Revision: November 24, 2026. D1–D15 preserve Austin’s November 16 rules with November 17 replacement entries D2, D4, D14, D15. Historical figures remain historical; current validation is data-v0.7 (320 tests at the November 27 freeze, 313 before pull request 148's sensitivity tests; 198 checks passed, 0 failed, 18 warnings). M1–M10 are newly assigned documentation IDs, not original tracker IDs.

## Austin Edwards — T65 decision register

Source: How Our Data Works, November 16, data-v0.6, commit 231281b, with November 17 replacement entries.

## D1 One set of metro boundaries
**Rule:** All 393 metros, built from their 1,252 counties with OMB's July 2023 definitions, applied to every year.
**Why:** A metro covers the same counties in 2015 as in 2024, so a trend is real change, not a moved border. No candidate market is screened out up front.
**Decided by:** BankUnited, 10/19: score all 393 metros (B9). Austin, as crosswalk owner: one 2023 vintage for every year.
**Alternatives:** Each year's own definitions; a regional subset, as in the 10/21 demos (124 Southeast and Mid-Atlantic metros).
**If it changed:** A new definition moves counties between metros in every table, so it calls for a new major data version, not a routine refresh.
**Limitation:** Older years won't match figures published under older definitions: Census's 2021 file for Charlotte is 380 establishments short, Anson County's.

## D2 Missing stays missing

**Rule:** A value the source doesn't report stays empty, never 0. Zeros a source uses to mean "not reported" are emptied too.

**Why:** A 0 reads as no activity and would drag a metro's or a bank's score down.

**Decided by:** Data engineering rule in the data dictionary; the last zero fixes shipped in data-v0.5 on 10/28 (B14).

**Alternatives:** Filling with 0, or estimating gaps in the data. Estimating is left to the scoring, which counts a missing local-lender growth as the 50th percentile. Since scoring v0.4 it also leaves a sector Census doesn't publish out of the industry HHI. The tables keep those cells empty; within that one measure, leaving a sector out works like counting it as 0.

**If it changed:** Zero-filling would score metros with gaps, such as Connecticut's, as weak instead of leaving them unranked.

**Limitation:** Every model has to handle blanks on purpose; 6 metros have a partial score in scoring v0.5: Connecticut's 5 and Eagle Pass, TX. Examples: Connecticut's BEA values before 2024, uninsured deposits at banks under $1 billion.

## D3 Counties summed into metros
**Rule:** Counts and dollars are summed from county to metro. Rates are computed after summing, never averaged across counties.
**Why:** Sums are exact. An average of county rates would weigh a small county the same as a large one.
**Decided by:** Austin and Bhavana, in the 9/28 source split; written into the data dictionary.
**Alternatives:** Averaging county rates; agencies' own metro files, which use whatever definitions were current when published.
**If it changed:** Little: Charlotte's 2023 establishment count matches Census's own metro file exactly, 71,411.
**Limitation:** A metro missing a county's figure is an undercount, and a count column shows how many counties reported. Charlotte 2023 has nonresidential construction for 10 of its 11 counties.

## D4 Withheld and unpublished cells

**Rule:** Cells Census or BLS withhold are left out of sums, not counted as 0. Exceptions: a withheld size class counts as 0 in the 20-to-249-employee count, and two withheld county-years in Kahului-Wailuku (2015 and 2016) read as 0.

**Why:** A withheld cell hides a real value, and 0 would understate it.

**Decided by:** Bhavana in the CBP and CRE builds (PRs #2 and #13), with Austin's reviews; the QCEW rule in PR #122, agreed 11/12.

**Alternatives:** Counting withheld cells as 0; estimating the hidden value.

**If it changed:** The 20-to-249 count runs short by up to 2 per withheld cell. Sector jobs and payroll for 2015 to 2017 run low where a county withheld them.

**Limitation:** From 2017, CBP omits county-sector rows under 3 establishments. In 2023, 95 metros lack at least one sector (mining in 69). Since scoring v0.4 (#128), their industry HHI uses the sectors Census publishes, which hold all but at most about 1% of their jobs; setting `[options] industry_hhi_missing_sectors` to `"blank"` restores the old rule.

## D5 Deposits booked at headquarters
**Rule:** Concentration is measured two ways: as reported, and without every main office and home-banking office. Deposit totals stay as FDIC reports them.
**Why:** Banks book deposits that aren't local at headquarters. In Charlotte, 84% of 2024's $457.3 billion sat at main offices, nearly all Bank of America's and Truist's.
**Decided by:** BankUnited on the 10/26 call: leave headquarters deposits out and say so in the docs (B10). Sonia and Matt added home-banking offices the same day.
**Alternatives:** As reported only; moving booked deposits back to branches, which public data don't allow.
**If it changed:** Charlotte 2024: HHI 5,391 and a 94% top-three share as reported, against 1,975 and 62% without those offices. Leaving out home-banking offices too changes 629 metro-years.
**Limitation:** A main office's local deposits are dropped along with the booked ones, so a bank headquartered in a metro is understated there.

## D6 Commercial loans over $1 million
**Rule:** Bank level only: C&I and nonfarm nonresidential loans minus the part with original amounts of $1 million or less (Call Report RC-C Part II). The scoring spreads each bank's loans across metros by its deposits outside headquarters.
**Why:** No public source has these loans by place, and CRA stops at $1 million.
**Decided by:** Austin found the measure, 10/15 (B4). BankUnited agreed to the deposit spread on the 10/26 call and confirmed on 10/29 that multifamily stays out.
**Alternatives:** A metro loan table in the pipeline, which Matt judged unneeded on 10/26.
**If it changed:** Matt's 10/26 test found the spread estimate over 95% correlated with metro payroll and deposits.
**Limitation:** A bank's lending needn't follow its deposits. Construction and multifamily loans have no size split, and smaller banks report the split only for June and December.

**November 24 reconciliation:** Current Pillar 1 uses all C&I (LNCI) and CRE construction, multifamily and nonfarm nonresidential loans, including owner-occupied, all sizes, for both allocated and local-lender measures. D6 records the October 29 exclusion of multifamily in the historical data-layer decision; scoring does not read D6 over-$1m fields.

**November 25 decision:** multifamily stays in Pillar 1's aggregate CRE (construction + multifamily + nonfarm nonresidential, all loan sizes), with no rerun. Akayiah Bell decided this in the team chat on November 25 (4:34 PM), after Matt D'Allaird's and Austin Edwards's review, and Elliot Leibowitz was informed. The HMDA multifamily and 5+ unit permit measures stay excluded. D6's October 29 exclusion applies only to the over-$1 million measures.

## D7 Commercial real estate by proxy
**Rule:** Real estate (NAICS 531) and nonresidential building construction (NAICS 2362): establishments, jobs and payroll from CBP, with QCEW filling missing cells and all of 2024.
**Why:** No public source has commercial vacancies, rents or sales by metro.
**Decided by:** BankUnited, 11/5: it found no metro-level CRE source, so CRE stays on public proxies (B8). Built by Bhavana (PR #2); Austin checked the licenses on 10/13.
**Alternatives:** S&P Capital IQ (BankUnited had no luck, 10/29); building permits (discussed 10/26); bank CRE loans spread by deposits, which Pillar 1 also uses.
**If it changed:** 2024 comes from QCEW, which counts differently: for Charlotte 2023 it ran 11% higher on real estate establishments and 38% on nonresidential construction. A 2023-to-2024 change is partly a change of source.
**Limitation:** NAICS 531 includes residential landlords. Business counts track activity, not prices or credit demand.

## D8 Small-business lending from CRA
**Rule:** CRA loans of $1 million or less, the three loan-size bands added together, by county and by lender.
**Why:** It is the only public small-business lending by place.
**Decided by:** BankUnited, 10/19: drop the size bands, since CRA matters once BankUnited is in a region, not as a reason to enter one (B7).
**Alternatives:** Keeping the three size bands.
**If it changed:** The bands split the same totals three ways, so the totals don't change.
**Limitation:** Only banks with $1.564 billion or more in assets must report (2024). They hold 77.6% of small business loans outstanding, so a lender's share is of what reporters lent.

## D9 Banks keyed on the RSSD ID
**Rule:** Every table keys banks on the Federal Reserve's RSSD ID and groups them into organizations by top holder. FDIC certificates are kept but never joined on.
**Why:** Every bank source carries the RSSD ID, and CRA carries nothing else. Certificates move in mergers: 15 moved between RSSD IDs in 2015 to 2026.
**Decided by:** Austin (T45, PR #93), approved by Bhavana 10/27 and merged 10/29.
**Alternatives:** FDIC certificates; bank names, which aren't unique (FIRST BCORP is two organizations).
**If it changed:** SOD and the Call Reports name the same top holder for 98.6% of bank-years (93.7% in 2015).
**Limitation:** Three standing check warnings come from mergers and filing quirks, such as Flagstar's 2022 offices listed under New York Community Bank.

## D10 Peer set
**Rule:** Organizations with $10 billion to $100 billion in combined bank assets: 126 organizations with 168 banks at June 30, 2026.
**Why:** It is BankUnited's size range: $34.86 billion at June 30, 2026.
**Decided by:** Elliot confirmed the pod's 10/15 proposal on 10/19 (B1).
**Alternatives:** Counting banks one by one: 133 banks in 129 organizations, adding Bank of America, BNY Mellon, Charles Schwab, RBC and TD and dropping Pinnacle Bancorp and Wintrust.
**If it changed:** Membership moves each quarter; python -m src.peers rewrites the list.
**Limitation:** It includes six insured U.S. branches of foreign banks, flagged in organization_type. The scores hold peers out as a check on the weights (pod meeting, 10/29).

## D11 Release dates for the back-test
**Rule:** release_dates.csv dates the first release of every source, dataset and year. A year is usable from its earliest release date, a Call Report from 35 days after its quarter ends.
**Why:** The Charlotte back-test may use only what was public before its decision date.
**Decided by:** Austin and Sonia agreed the five rules on 10/15 (T52); Bhavana added the dictionary's Released column (PR #97, 10/29).
**Alternatives:** Keeping each release's values as first published, which the tables don't: they hold the latest revisions.
**If it changed:** The back-test uses revised numbers on first-release timing. BEA's November 2023 revision of county income, for one, reached back to 1979.
**Limitation:** Where no first-release date turned up, the row carries the earliest date the data was provably public, an upper bound.

## D12 BEA's combined county areas
**Rule:** BEA reports 23 Virginia counties together with their independent cities (codes 519xx), and Maui with Kalawao (15901). Each code goes to the metro of its parts.
**Why:** Left out, they cost data-v0.3 29% of Washington's GDP and every BEA value for Harrisonburg, Staunton and Kahului-Wailuku.
**Decided by:** Found in Austin's reviews, 10/19 and 10/21; fixed by Bhavana in PR #14, approved 10/21, released in data-v0.4.
**Alternatives:** Leaving them out, as data-v0.3 did.
**If it changed:** Washington's 2023 GDP is $708.16 billion with them and $501.25 billion without; 12 metros change.
**Limitation:** Codes in a micropolitan area or outside any metro don't reach the tables.

## D13 BEA history to 2010
**Rule:** BEA's 2010 to 2014 values sit in their own table, msa_year_history, with the same metros and columns.
**Why:** The ML pod asked for history back to 2010 for its volatility measures, and only BEA reaches back that far.
**Decided by:** The ML pod at the 10/21 meeting; shipped in data-v0.5 (PR #92).
**Alternatives:** Shorter windows, which the ML pod said it could work with.
**If it changed:** 2013 is a real dip in personal income, falling in 108 of 382 metros, so a window that includes it reads more volatile.
**Limitation:** 382 of the 393 metros have history: none in Connecticut or Puerto Rico.

**November 24 reconciliation:** Evan confirms GDP volatility uses nine annual growth rates 2016–2024; the baseline uses no BEA years before 2015; back-dated runs may use 2010–2014 history.

**D13 clarification:** The baseline uses no BEA years before 2015; the 2010–2014 history is used only by back-dated runs. GDP volatility uses nine annual rates, 2016–2024.

## D14 A map point for every metro

**Rule:** Each metro's Census Gazetteer internal point (2026 file), the same in every year.

**Why:** One free file covers all 393 metros for the Fit & Feasibility distance filter.

**Decided by:** Built by Austin at Matt's and Akayiah's request, 11/12 (T80, data-v0.6); the ML pod accepted internal points on 11/14.

**Alternatives:** 2020 population centers, which can't be matched to Connecticut's new regions.

**If it changed:** Points sit a median 6.7 miles from population centers, over 50 for 7 metros. Two metros that would otherwise rank sit just outside ML's 500-mile filter: Detroit (503 miles) and El Paso (508).

**Limitation:** A geographic center, not where people live; distances are straight-line. The distance filter is in main since #128 (11/16): off in the baseline, 500 miles in the Adjacency scenario.


## D15 BankUnited's own footprint

**Rule:** The `bankunited_` columns come from the SOD offices and CRA loans of BankUnited, N.A. (RSSD 3938186).

**Why:** Both are public by metro and year from 2015.

**Decided by:** Austin (PR #91, data-v0.5).

**Alternatives:** BankUnited's own announcements, which the back-test needs for entry dates anyway.

**If it changed:** The Fit filters (#128) count 13 BankUnited markets: the 10 branch markets in the 2024 deposit survey plus the office-only Atlanta, Charlotte and Houston, added by hand. An as-of run leaves out Atlanta before 4/7/2022 and Charlotte before 7/17/2025.

**Limitation:** An office with no deposits or few CRA loans doesn't show: the Atlanta corporate banking office, opened April 2022, isn't in SOD through June 2024.


# ML and scoring decisions

## M1 Balanced pillar weights

**Rule:** 25% each; metric weights normalized; pillar percentiles combined.

**Why:** Equal starting point; adjustable for strategic priorities.

**Evidence:** Baseline configuration; Matt

**Alternatives:** Alternative pillar weights

**Impact / limitation:** Ranks may change; not calibrated to profitability.

## M2 Population floor

**Rule:** 250,000; zero disables.

**Why:** Minimum market scale.

**Evidence:** Nov 6 gate; Austin Nov 17

**Alternatives:** No floor

**Impact / limitation:** 190 ranked; 191 complete below floor.

## M3 Fit filters

**Rule:** Industry percentile default 0; distance and existing-market exclusion off; Adjacency 500 miles.

**Why:** Separate strategic fit from attractiveness.

**Evidence:** Elliot Nov 24; PR #128

**Alternatives:** Different thresholds

**Impact / limitation:** Eligibility only; unknown industry shares and straight-line distance limitations.

## M4 Lending scope

**Rule:** 20–249 employees; owner-occupied CRE included; all loan sizes.

**Why:** Public-data proxy and target franchise alignment.

**Evidence:** Matt / sponsor Nov 24

**Alternatives:** 20–499 or >$1M

**Impact / limitation:** Establishments not firms; bank-wide loans allocated by deposits.

## M5 Local lenders

**Rule:** 50% domestic deposit threshold; fifth-highest growth cap 191%; both measures weighted; neutral 50 percentile fill when configured.

**Why:** Limit extreme growth and retain sparse markets.

**Evidence:** Elliot Nov 24; prior chapter

**Alternatives:** 25% cap; no fill; zero weights

**Impact / limitation:** Neutral fill applies to missing local-lender measures.

## M6 Diagnostics

**Rule:** Four zero-weight metrics retained; competition × growth also zero baseline, 80% in dedicated scenario.

**Why:** Preserve optional analysis.

**Evidence:** Matt and Jainesh Nov 24

**Alternatives:** Remove or weight diagnostics

**Impact / limitation:** Scenario not baseline; no win-rate calibration.

## M7 Industry HHI

**Rule:** 2023 CBP classified employment; omit suppressed sectors under v0.4.

**Why:** Avoid losing entire metro for small missing sectors.

**Evidence:** PR #128; Evan Nov 24

**Alternatives:** Blank entire HHI

**Impact / limitation:** Historical 14 additional ranked metros.

## M8 Pillar 3

**Rule:** Five lower-is-better metrics, 20% each; fixed 2021 leaders through 2024.

**Why:** Measure deposit contestability.

**Evidence:** Jainesh Nov 24

**Alternatives:** Competition × growth scenario

**Impact / limitation:** Deposit not loan rivalry; mergers distort share.

## M9 Pillar 4

**Rule:** Eight metrics, 12.5% each; Census population/migration; establishment growth proxy.

**Why:** Assess durability.

**Evidence:** Evan, November 24

**Alternatives:** QCEW HHI or separate formation measure

**Impact / limitation:** QCEW additions supplementary.

## M10 Sensitivity and release evidence

**Rule:** Scoring v0.5 sensitivity retains 23–25 of the original top 25; 320 tests at the freeze (313 before pull request 148); 198 checks passed, 0 failed, 18 warnings.

**Why:** Document robustness and validation.

**Evidence:** Matt’s final v0.5 sensitivity figures communicated November 25; Austin’s November 24 rerun on main 546f659; reproduced by `python -m src.pillar_sensitivity` (pull request 148), output `outputs/sensitivity/pillar_metric_sensitivity.csv`

**Alternatives:** Alternative weights and removals

**Impact / limitation:** Austin reran both tests and checks. Matt D’Allaird’s final scoring v0.5 sensitivity analysis, confirmed November 25, retained 23–25 of the original top 25 markets when individual measures were removed. Similarity ranged from 0.989 to 0.999; the largest single-measure movement was 26 places (middle-market growth), and the maximum movement under ±25% weight changes was 13 places. Repository drop-measure scenarios are separate: 23–24 on main and 22–24 on the v0.5 branch (Austin, November 24).
